ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a circular polar projection schematic diagram. There is a pole position near the center of the circle, and the outer ring is the boundary of the great circle; point A is on the outer ring at the very top of the circle, and point P is on a horizontal line slightly left of the center of the circle; the lower-left side of the figure is marked “180°”, and the terminator line is a curved line and is tangent to the polar circle at point P. Then reason: The stem says that at this time London is Saturday, while Beijing is already Sunday. Beijing is located east of London, indicating that the date enters the next day earlier toward the east. Combined with the 180° meridian marking in the figure, it can be determined that this polar projection is a view from above the South Pole, and on this basis the direction in which longitude increases eastward is determined. In a South Pole projection, the farther away from the center of the circle, the more northward it is; point A is farther outward than point P, so A is north of P. Comparing according to the already determined longitude direction, point A is also east of point P. Combining the north-south and east-west directions, point A is located northeast of point P.

Then compare positions: since A is farther from the South Pole center than P, A is north of P; using the established longitude sense, A lies east of P. Combine the two components to answer that A is northeast of P.
